toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: Collected 0 of the 2 allowed catalogue items. The initial evidence (E1-E6) already settles the sign-off decision. The two open questions are why the single QC result failed and what exactly drives the Ward 6 highs. Neither would change that decision, and the Ward 6 question is best settled by fresh repeat samples rather than more records.
output.brief:
Dr Marrable: one potassium control result on Analyzer B (3.8 standard deviations high) was out of range. It looks like a one-off, not a failing analyzer or bad reagent lot. The other control levels and sodium/chloride passed; the repeat twenty minutes later passed; control averages haven't moved since the lot change; 43 patient samples re-run on Analyzer A agreed within 0.10 mmol/L; patient averages are steady. Logs show every scheduled control ran on time, so the staffing suspicion isn't supported. Whether a sampling glitch or chance caused it can't be told; don't record a cause as confirmed.

Ward 6's highs are split evenly across both analyzers, and most had long transport delays since the tube outage. That points to delay (renal transfers may add), but nobody has re-sampled those patients, so it isn't proven.

Sign off: return B to service; close the review with no amendments; no recall, quarantine or wider limits. Extra control checks for a week are optional. Today: get fresh repeat samples from the 14 Ward 6 patients and speed up transport. Confidence: high on the analyzer, moderate on Ward 6; more evidence wouldn't change this decision.
